page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8ia.16xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated instance designed for compute-intensive workloads that require moderate hardware acceleration alongside substantial CPU and system memory resources. Running on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, this instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processors clocked at 3.4 GHz across 64 vCPUs. It is paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 6.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L20 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of VRAM. This configuration offers significant graphic and tensor compute capacity without the overhead of multi-GPU topologies. The instance does not include bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on networked block storage for persistent data requirements. Network performance is anchored by a high-throughput 40 Gbps baseline interface, ensuring efficient transport for data ingestion and inter-service communication.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn8ia.16xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for systems that need a dedicated enterprise GPU without the cost footprint of high-end distributed training clusters. The combination of a single 48 GB L20 GPU, high CPU density, and 384 GB of host RAM makes it well fitted for large language model inference, AI-powered video processing, deep learning model evaluation, and memory-heavy scientific batch processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8ia.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9T34 processors running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 384.0 GB of host RAM, delivering 6.0 GB of memory per core, and is equipped with a single NVIDIA L20 GPU featuring 48 GB of Ada Lovelace VRAM. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, while offering a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This architecture yields a balanced resource density, making it cost-efficient for single-accelerator workloads that still demand high-capacity host memory and strong CPU parallelization. Primary workloads include deep learning inference, data processing pipelines, rendering tasks, and AI model evaluation.
